changes.text: @kemppelinvestments-del thanks for the test funds. The evaluator is now staked at the registry minimum (2.00 USDC on Base Sepolia, [tx](https://sepolia.basescan.org/tx/0x45d2d0ea9779861f21d846359cd98877457679b94a636cc0df1ed57e52274fca)), so it can take job 1. Post the job and its acceptance criteria, and the verdict will go on-chain with the `receipt_sha256` of the signed acceptance record it is based on, so anyone can check the verdict against the record offline.

changes.author: payload-tools
changes.text: The verdict function makes the gap concrete. On a Partial outcome, payoutBps sets how much is released and reasonHash can point back to the acceptance record, but neither checks the percentage against the entitlement it is supposed to reflect. If the percentage were tied to an entitlement record fixed before payment, the escrow would have something to verify the number against, not just somewhere to store it.

changes.author: kemppelinvestments-del
changes.text:
@payload-tools agreed, that's a real gap. Today `payoutBps` on a Partial outcome is trusted as the evaluator's number, and `reasonHash` only lets anyone check it afterwards against the signed acceptance record. The escrow doesn't check it on-chain.

The fix we're looking at is committing a payout schedule at funding time: a hash of the criteria plus the allowed `payoutBps` for each outcome, stored on the job. `verdict` would then reject any percentage that doesn't match the schedule for the outcome the record gives.
